newsitem.title: POLAND: PROTESTS GROWING AGAINST NEW POLISH CONSTITUION.
newsitem.headline: PROTESTS GROWING AGAINST NEW POLISH CONSTITUION.

text.p: Opposition to Poland's new draft constitution appeared to mount on Saturday, as Poles celebrated their national day commemorating Europe's first written constitution.

Roman Catholic Leader Jozef Glemp accused the constitution's authors of insensitivity to believers, while the country's major right-wing opposition party announced it had collected half a million signatures in support of an alternative draft.

Addressing 100,000 worshippers in the southern town of Czestochowa, the cardinal called the creators of the draft "mostly non-believers, aliens and the (religiously) frigid...who do not understand the believing majority," PAP news agency reported.
National day, marking the anniversary of Poland's 1791 Constitution, is celebrated by the Church as the feastday of Our Lady Queen of Poland.
The new constitution, passed by parliament on April 2, was a compromise hammered out by two leftist coalition parties with communist-era roots and two opposition parties.
Poles will be able to vote on it in a popular referendum set for May 25.

The Reconstruction of Poland (ROP) movement announced that 500,000 people had signed its petition to give voters a choice between parliament's draft and a more Catholic-minded version drawn up by the right-leaning Solidarity trade-union movement.
As things now stand, the referendum will allow voters only to approve or reject the single parliamentary draft.
In Warsaw, a group of war veterans celebrating Polish national day called on Poles to vote against the constitution.
"Let's not allow ourselves to be deceived," World War Two resistance fighter Antoni Heda said at a rally. "This constitution is against the Polish nation, it is for atheists and communistic masons."
Earlier in the day, ex-communist President Aleksander Kwasniewski extolled the new constitution as the basis of "a modern, common and truly democratic state."

As he spoke at national day celebrations near Warsaw's Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, right-wing activists in Krakow scuffled with police to prevent a prominent ex-communist laying a wreath at a memorial honouring Polish vicitms of Soviet atrocities.
The leader of the rightist Republican League was hurt in the fray and two people were detained in the southern city, private Radio Zet reported.
Andrzej Urbanczyk, spokesman of the ex-communist Democratic left Alliance (SLD) had to duck flying eggs and run for cover after laying his wreath.
"We cannot permit any organisation linked to the SLD to desecrate this cross of national memory by laying flowers here," PAP quoted Jerzy Bukowski, leader of an ex-servicemen's group, as saying.
The ageing ex-servicemen had joined backers of the youthful Republican League and ROP in trying to break through a police cordon shielding Urbanczyk.
